chapter: Writing, Oklahoma roots and the origins of bebop
title: Christian's unamplified playing, Goodman and Minton's
summary: He played an acoustic guitar then; Minton's kept an amp for him.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: What was I talking about? We were in Oklahoma City, right?
Well, he was something, boy. I really loved him. When I heard him, I couldn't hardly believe that a man could sound that good, you know. But he was really taking care of business when I met him.
Did he already have that kind of linear style going?

Oh yeah, he had that going. But he didn't have an electric amp. He just had a plain guitar. And he made that thing sing. People would come down to hear him play that, man. But with the electric guitar, I imagine he might have went further. Who knows? But they didn't have such things -- down in Oklahoma anyway. And if they did have them, I doubt whether he had the money enough to bbuy one.
But then eventually he did get one, and...

Oh, he did get one. When he got with Goodman, I mean... Well, he had one before that. But when he got with Goodman, that really just let him be free as he wanted to be. Because he had a good instrument, and Goodman was featuring him, letting him play -- and he was playing.
Do you remember him at Minton's?
Yeah, I used to go up there all the time. That used to be a hangout. Prez used to go up there, and Bird and Dizzy and Monk -- all the guys used to go by there.
Well, the story has been told that they kept an amplifier for him so that he could go and just plug in after he finished with Goodman down at the Paramount...
Then he wouldn't have to lug the amplifier, just bring his guitar and...
Well, that was nice. Whoever thought of that was nice. I like people that think of nice things to do for other people.
